correction: The official final Council legislative act and the addressed German government memorandum describe an18-month period after entry into force of the specified delegated and implementing acts. The German memorandum physical115explicitly says those acts are not yet available and lists Commission adoption deadlines of1January2028and1January2030respectively. A fixed1July2029start does not follow simply by adding18months to the first adoption deadline. Adoption and entry into force are also distinct.
effect: An unconditional statutory-start reading overstates timetable certainty and could compress the preparation horizon. A planning assumption about early secondary acts could nevertheless yield a2029date; no actual future commencement date is established here.
limits: Unresolved rather than a proved calendar-date error. The author may be using a conventional expected schedule, and early national reform may be independently warranted. This does not prove a2031start, an inevitable delay, or that the requested fee differentiation is inappropriate. It does not assume the acts must be adopted exactly on their deadlines. No intent is inferred.
context_and_alternatives: Read the complete six-page official submission. The next sentence calls for developing and testing a functioning model in time, which is consistent with a forward-looking planning argument. The narrow lead concerns the unqualified statutory attribution, not disagreement with that policy.
